opening: Lord, meet us gently today and always
body:
“His searching glance is on mankind.” What an easy sentence to glaze over, yet what it contains is profound. Jesus sees deeper than surface behavior. Throughout the Gospel of John, He knew the disciples intensely — Peter’s fear and devotion, Thomas’ doubt and sincerity, John’s love, Judas’ unrest, Nicodemus’ searching heart. These were never just observations. Christ’s gaze revealed, called, corrected, restored, and drew each person toward deeper union with Him. With the Resurrection, the Spirit of Truth was sent to guide humanity toward all truth. These profound realities should move us to get ourselves together spiritually, to grow in union with Kyrios, with Maran, the Lord who came to humanity to draw us near to Himself.

His gaze is upon us now, searching hearts and guiding us toward Truth. It is an invitation to cross-examine our spiritual condition, to find His love and go there, remain there, and bring others there also. Christ descended to us in human likeness to gather His people, teach His people, and shepherd His people. We are meant to walk this journey with Him, allowing Him to gaze upon us, to learn our souls and what they resonate with, and to guide us toward His purpose so that we are never separated from His Truth. Allowing ourselves to be fully seen by God is not a favor to Him — God already knows you completely. It is humanity that hides, doubts, distances itself, or convinces itself it is anonymous. Do not allow yourself the easy way out. Loving and believing in God is not the lonely path; separation from Him is.
